title: Weak Prompt, Strong Prompt
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Two prompt cards side by side, each divided into the five parts of a prompt; the weak card fills one band and leaves four empty, and the strong card fills all five.

educational.topic: The five parts of a rubric prompt: role, task, input, rules, and output format
learningObjectives: The learner will evaluate a prompt against the five parts of a rubric prompt and name the part that is missing.
prerequisites: Prompts and the parts of a rubric prompt from [Chapter 12](../../chapters/12-ai-agents-prompts-scoring/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a reference picture, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: Which of the five bands is empty?
What should the model write when it cannot tell?
commonMisconceptions: A short prompt is a good prompt
A good prompt guarantees a good answer
assessmentOpportunities: Which part tells the model what to do when it cannot tell?
Why does the strong prompt include the full text of the resource?
Does a strong prompt guarantee a correct answer?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz buttons
controls.description: switch between exploring the poster and answering quiz questions.

controls.name: Poster zones
controls.description: hover or press to read about that part of the poster. In quiz mode a press is your answer.

controls.name: Try Again
controls.description: repeats the quiz after the last question.
